plan: This is a second-price sealed-bid auction (Vickrey auction) with 3 bidders. In such auctions, bidding your true value is a dominant strategy - it maximizes expected profit regardless of what other bidders do. If I win, I pay the second-highest bid, not my own bid, so there's no incentive to shade my bid down, and bidding higher than my value risks negative profit. Therefore, I should bid exactly my value of $25.

In a second-price sealed-bid auction, bidding your true value is the dominant strategy regardless of what others do. If I win, I pay the second-highest bid (not my own bid), so bidding above or below my value only risks either winning at a loss or losing profitable opportunities. With a value of $3, bidding exactly $3 ensures I only win when profitable (paying less than $3) and never overpay.

In a second-price auction, bidding your true value is a dominant strategy regardless of the number of bidders or their strategies. This is because you pay the second-highest bid, not your own bid, so overbidding risks paying more than the item is worth, while underbidding risks losing profitable opportunities. Since my value is $26, I should bid exactly $26 to maximize expected profit.
